title: Midweek Reflection Rituals & Evidence Log
content:
Purpose: quick midweek checkpoint to capture small wins, friction, and concrete evidence for 1:1s or self-review. Keep short, habitual.

How I use this file: open Wednesday morning, spend 15–25 minutes. Capture 3 things: (A) wins that map to goals; (B) blockers that are actionable; (C) ask for manager or follow-up items.

Template I follow (very terse):
- Week: YYYY-WW -> fill each time
- Theme / focus for the week: single sentence
- 3 evidence bullets (what changed / shipped / influenced)
- 2 micro-blockers (what I need to remove or escalate)
- 1 experiment I ran or plan to try next 7 days
- Manager asks (explicit, small, timeboxed)

--- example entry (fresh) ---
Week: 2026-02 
Theme: Scale interview scorecard rollout to Sales hires
Evidence:
- Finalized alpha scorecard questions; shared doc with hiring-panel (link: /confluence/hiring-scorecard).
- Ran 2 calibration sessions with SE recruiting; collected 6 calibrated notes -> average deviation down 18% (rough calc).
- Drafted one-pager for hiring directors; received verbal buy-in in sync (action: add timeline & metrics).
Micro-blockers:
- Need final alignment on required competencies from Sales leadership (waiting on Sarah).
- Recruiting backlog for Feb means panel bandwidth limited next week (may delay pilot).
Experiment:
- Try a 20-minute async calibration using Miro + 3 sample interviews to see if alignment can be done without an all-hands meeting.
Manager asks:
- Can you pull Sarah into a 15-min sync with me this week? (aim: finalize competencies).
- Approve moving 3 candidate interviews into pilot panel (I can coordinate).

--- freeform scratch / quick notes ---
Observations:
- When I narrate the tradeoffs out loud (cost vs speed vs precision) stakeholders respond faster. Keep doing mini-frames in syncs.
- My focus drift shows up as long email threads rather than short asks; experiment: always end with 2 bullet asks in emails.

Snippets to copy into 1:1 (concise):
- "Two wins: scorecard alpha complete; calibration session run with recruiting. Two small risks: need Sales competency confirmation + recruiting capacity for pilot. Ask: 15-min alignment with Sarah and approval to book pilot interviews."

Backlog (capture, then prune):
- Update example interview rubric with sales-specific metrics (metric: discovery depth).
- Create playbook stub for panel calibration (1-pager).
- Pull historical data on time-to-hire for Sales to set pilot KPI.

Evidence fridge (short, verifiable artifacts I can drop into self-review):
- doc: /confluence/hiring-scorecard (alpha)
- meeting notes: 2026-02-10 calibration-notes (in my drive)
- slack thread: #recruiting-sales-calibration (pinned messages)

Quick habit cues (how I keep this live):
- Wednesday morning: 8:30am — open this file, write 3 evidence bullets.
- Thursday: add any new micro-blockers.
- Friday morning: distill to 1-2 lines for weekly sync and add to weekly update.

Micro-routines to improve signal:
- At end of any meeting where a decision is expected, write 1-line outcome + next step in notes.
- When I get positive feedback, capture it immediately (one sentence + who said it).

Notes to self (raw, unpolished):
- don’t over-index on perfection for scorecard; we need iterative data.
- remember: alignment is social work — make it easy to say yes.
- track time spent across hiring workstreams this month (to argue for FTE or contractor help).

Open questions / unresolved:
- If Sales leadership prefers a different framing of competencies, how quickly can the pilot pivot? (need decision window)
- What is the minimal acceptable panel size to avoid noisy signals?

Quick wins to capture before next 1:1:
- Send Sarah a short 3-bullet note and 2 time options (15-min).
- Create pilot calendar invites (block slots) and share with recruiting to confirm panel availability.
- Draft measurement plan (3 KPIs: calibration deviation, time-to-hire, offer-accept rate)

Meta: why this works for me
- Small, frequent snapshots lower my cognitive overhead during reviews.
- Having explicit "manager asks" forces clarity and action.
- The discipline of capturing evidence prevents the fuzzy memory problem in performance conversations.

TODO (now):
- [ ] Send Sarah note (today)
- [ ] Block pilot interview slots (EOD Wednesday)
- [ ] Upload calibration notes to confluence (this week)

End of entry.

---- older seed entries (choppy) ----
2025-11 Week: focus on early-career L&D -> ran 3 office hours, documented 7 common questions, started FAQ
2025-07 Week: org-wide offsite prep -> pulled 6 engagement signals, proposed 3 breakout formats, ask: budget for facilitator -> pending

Capture style note: keep sentences short. Use this as the canonical midweek log. If something is big, spin a new doc (project doc).

Version history: personal; if I ever share, prune the raw 'open questions' before handing off.

[handy copy for weekly update]
- Progress: alpha scorecard + calibration session completed.
- Risk: waiting on Sales competency confirmation; recruiting capacity constraints.
- Ask: 15-min alignment with Sarah + approval to move 3 interviews into pilot.
